name: MiniMax
intro: MiniMax went from $79M of total 2025 revenue — disclosed in its Hong Kong IPO prospectus — to more than $800M of annualized recurring revenue by August 2026, with roughly 80% from enterprise customers. Every reported figure below is traced to filings, Dealroom and 36Kr; HKD/RMB figures are converted to USD.

modelTitle: How Enterprise Contracts Outgrew the Consumer Apps.
modelParagraphs: MiniMax runs a multi-modal portfolio — the MiniMax LLMs (M2/M2.5), Hailuo video, and consumer apps like Talkie — monetized through a token-based API, enterprise contracts, and subscription apps. Enterprise is now the engine: roughly 80% of the August 2026 ARR, up from over 60% of H1 2026 revenue, sold as direct model access and agent deployments.

Notably, open-sourcing M2 and M2.5 — and cutting M2.5 inference costs by more than 50% — has so far grown rather than cannibalized revenue, as enterprise adoption followed the models. The 2025 base was still thin ($79M of revenue at a 25.4% gross margin, against ~$180M of nine-month R&D spend), which makes the 2026 ARR ramp the decisive test.
revenueMix: ~80% of ARR — direct contracts and agent deployments on MiniMax and M-series models.
Self-serve developer access across text, video (Hailuo) and audio models.
Talkie and companion products; historically the largest consumer line.

faqs.a: MiniMax's annualized recurring revenue surpassed $800 million in August 2026, per its H1 2026 reporting, with roughly 80% coming from enterprise customers. Management projects $800M–$1B ARR for full-year 2026 — nearly 20x its total 2025 revenue.

faqs.q: How Much Revenue Did MiniMax Report Before the ARR Surge?
faqs.a: Per its Hong Kong IPO prospectus: $3.5M in 2023, $30.5M in 2024 (~9x growth), and $79M in 2025 (+159% YoY) at a 25.4% gross margin. Those are audited revenue figures, not ARR.

Token-based API access to its M-series language models plus Hailuo video and audio models, enterprise model deployments, and consumer subscription apps such as Talkie. Enterprise is now the dominant line.

faqs.q: Did Open-Sourcing Its Models Hurt MiniMax's Revenue?
faqs.a: No — open-sourcing M2 and M2.5, alongside cutting M2.5 inference costs by more than 50%, coincided with accelerating enterprise adoption. ARR kept climbing to $800M+ after the open-source pivot.

MiniMax listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in January 2026, raising up to roughly $539 million, and trades at a market capitalization around HK$81 billion as of 2026. It is also pursuing an A-share listing.
